questions.text: मानव में, औसत जीन में क्षारकों (बेस) की संख्या (i) तथा सबसे बड़े मानव जीन में क्षारकों (बेस) की संख्या (ii) होती है। रिक्त स्थान (i) तथा (ii) के लिए सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए।
questions.text_english: In a human, the average gene consists of (i) bases and the largest known human gene contains (ii) bases. Select the correct option to fill in the blanks (i) and (ii).
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A): the average human gene consists of about 800 bases, while the largest known human gene — the dystrophin gene — contains approximately 1.6 million base pairs. Option (C) overstates the average gene size (8000 bases is too high for an average gene), and option (D) gives incorrect values entirely. Option (B) gives values far too small for both.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है: मानव में औसत जीन में लगभग 800 क्षारक होते हैं, जबकि सबसे बड़े ज्ञात मानव जीन — डिस्ट्रोफिन जीन — में लगभग 1.6 मिलियन क्षार युगल होते हैं।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा जीव (प्राणी) अमीबता (अमीबिएसिस) रोग का संवाहक है?
questions.text_english: Which of the following is a carrier for the disease Amoebiasis?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Housefly. Amoebiasis is caused by Entamoeba histolytica and is transmitted through contaminated food and water. The housefly (Musca domestica) acts as a mechanical carrier by sitting on infected faecal matter and then on food. Culex mosquito transmits filariasis, female Anopheles transmits malaria, and snails are intermediate hosts for Schistosoma and liver flukes, not amoebiasis.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) घरेलू मक्खी है। अमीबिएसिस एंटअमीबा हिस्टोलिटिका के कारण होता है और घरेलू मक्खी इसकी यांत्रिक संवाहक है।

questions.text: प्रतिबंधन एंजाइम हिंड S2I में I क्या इंगित करता है?
questions.text_english: What does I in restriction enzyme Hind S2I indicate?

options.A: यह प्रथम न्यूक्लियोटाइड के बाद प्रतिबंधन स्थल पर काटता है।
options.B: यह जीवाणु के S2 प्रभेद से विलगित (पृथक्कृत) किया जाने वाला सबसे पहला एंजाइम था।
options.C: S2 प्रभेद से प्लास्मिड का पाचन करने हेतु केवल एक एंजाइम का उपयोग किया जा सकता है।
options.D: इस जीवाणु से केवल एक प्रतिबंधन एंजाइम ही पृथक किया गया है।

options_english.A: It cuts after the first nucleotide in the restriction site.
options_english.B: It is the first enzyme isolated from strain S2 of bacterium.
options_english.C: Only one enzyme can be used to digest a plasmid from S2 strain.
options_english.D: Only one restriction enzyme has been isolated from this bacteria.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). In the nomenclature of restriction enzymes, the Roman numeral (I, II, III…) indicates the order in which the enzyme was isolated from a particular strain of bacterium. HindIII means it was the third enzyme isolated from Haemophilus influenzae strain Rd. Similarly, HindS2I (or HindII) was the first enzyme isolated from strain S2. The letters do not indicate the cut position, the number of enzymes usable, or that only one enzyme exists from that bacterium.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है। प्रतिबंधन एंजाइम के नामकरण में रोमन अंक (I, II, III…) यह दर्शाता है कि वह एंजाइम उस जीवाणु के प्रभेद से किस क्रम में पृथक किया गया था।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित पौधों के उस जोड़े वाले सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए जिनमें जल द्वारा परागण होता है।
questions.text_english: Select the correct option for the pair of plants pollinated by water.

options.D: वाटर हायसिंथ तथा जल कुमुदिनी (वाटर लिली)

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Vallisneria and Hydrilla. Both are submerged aquatic plants that undergo hydrophily (pollination by water). Vallisneria releases male flowers that float to the surface and reach female flowers; Hydrilla is also pollinated under water. Zostera is a marine hydrophyte that is also water-pollinated, but Water lily is pollinated by insects (entomophily), not water. Parthenium is wind-pollinated (anemophily), and Water hyacinth is insect-pollinated.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) वैलिसनेरिया और हाइड्रिला है। दोनों जलमग्न पादप हैं जिनमें जलपरागण (हाइड्रोफिली) होता है।

questions.text: ड्रग तथा ऐल्कोहॉल के विषय में कुछ कथन नीचे दिए गए हैं: (i) किशोर मित्रों के दबाव (प्रभाव) में अधिक शीघ्र आ जाते हैं। (ii) ड्रग की लत के परिणामस्वरूप हमारे शरीर में उपस्थित संवेदीग्राहियों के प्रति सहनशीलता अधिक हो जाती है। (iii) ऐल्कोहॉल केन्द्रीय तंत्रिका तंत्र को प्रभावित करता है। (iv) ड्रग के अत्यधिक उपयोग से ऊर्जा शक्ति बढ़ाने में सहायता मिलती है। (v) उपचयी स्टेरॉइड्स आक्रामकता का अवनमन (कम) करते हैं। सही कथन/कथनों वाले विकल्प का चयन कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Some statements regarding drugs and alcohol are given below: (i) Adolescents are more vulnerable to peer pressure. (ii) Drug addiction leads to increased tolerance level of the receptors present in our body. (iii) Alcohol affects the central nervous system. (iv) Excessive use of drugs helps to increase energy. (v) Anabolic steroids decrease aggressiveness. Choose the option with correct statement(s).
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). Statement (i) is correct — adolescents are indeed more susceptible to peer pressure due to curiosity and the need for social acceptance. Statement (ii) is correct — repeated drug use causes the receptors to become less sensitive, requiring higher doses to achieve the same effect (tolerance). Statement (iii) is correct — alcohol is a CNS depressant. Statement (iv) is incorrect — excessive drug use causes physical and mental damage, not energy enhancement. Statement (v) is incorrect — anabolic steroids actually increase aggression and mood swings.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है। कथन (i), (ii) और (iii) सही हैं। अनाबोलिक स्टेरॉइड्स आक्रामकता बढ़ाते हैं, घटाते नहीं; और ड्रग के अत्यधिक उपयोग से ऊर्जा नहीं बढ़ती।

questions.text: किसी संतति में परीक्षार्थ एक संकर क्रॉस में किसी प्रभावी विशेषक के अभिव्यक्त (परिलक्षित) होने की न्यूनतम संभावना क्या होगी?
questions.text_english: What would be the minimum possibility of a dominant trait being expressed in an offspring after a monohybrid test cross?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) 50%. In a monohybrid test cross, a heterozygous dominant individual (Aa) is crossed with a homozygous recessive individual (aa). The offspring ratio is 50% Aa (dominant phenotype) and 50% aa (recessive phenotype). Therefore, the minimum probability of the dominant trait being expressed is 50%. If the individual being tested is homozygous dominant (AA), then 100% offspring show the dominant trait. The question asks for the minimum, which is 50%.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) 50% है। परीक्षार्थ एक संकर क्रॉस (Aa × aa) में 50% संतति Aa (प्रभावी लक्षण) और 50% aa (अप्रभावी लक्षण) होती है। अतः न्यूनतम संभावना 50% है।

questions.text: नीचे दिए गए आरेखों द्वारा चार विभिन्न अनुलेखन इकाइयों को दर्शाया गया है। उचित प्रकार से अभिचित्रित विकल्प का चयन कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Four different transcription units are shown below. Choose the option with the correct image.

options.A: समापक बाईं ओर, उन्नायक दाईं ओर; टेम्पलेट रज्जुक 3'→5' दिशा में; कोडिंग रज्जुक 5'→3' दिशा में
options.B: उन्नायक बाईं ओर, समापक दाईं ओर; टेम्पलेट रज्जुक 5'→3' दिशा में; कोडिंग रज्जुक 3'→5' दिशा में
options.C: उन्नायक बाईं ओर, समापक दाईं ओर; टेम्पलेट रज्जुक 3'→5' दिशा में; कोडिंग रज्जुक 5'→3' दिशा में
options.D: उन्नायक बाईं ओर, समापक दाईं ओर; कोडिंग रज्जुक 3'→5' दिशा में; टेम्पलेट रज्जुक 5'→3' दिशा में

options_english.A: Terminator on left, Promoter on right; Template strand runs 3' to 5'; Coding strand runs 5' to 3'
options_english.B: Promoter on left, Terminator on right; Template strand runs 5' to 3'; Coding strand runs 3' to 5'
options_english.C: Promoter on left, Terminator on right; Template strand runs 3' to 5'; Coding strand runs 5' to 3'
options_english.D: Promoter on left, Terminator on right; Coding strand runs 3' to 5'; Template strand runs 5' to 3'

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). In a transcription unit, the promoter is located upstream (towards the 3' end of the template strand) and the terminator is downstream (towards the 5' end of the template strand). RNA polymerase reads the template strand in the 3'→5' direction and synthesises mRNA in the 5'→3' direction. Option C correctly places the promoter on the left with the template strand running 3'→5' and the coding strand running 5'→3'. Option A has the promoter and terminator reversed. Options B and D have incorrect polarity of one or both strands.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) है। अनुलेखन इकाई में उन्नायक 3' सिरे की ओर और समापक 5' सिरे की ओर होता है। RNA पॉलिमरेज टेम्पलेट रज्जुक को 3'→5' दिशा में पढ़ता है।

questions.text: स्त्रियों (मानव मादा) में गर्भ उत्क्षेपण प्रतिवर्ता (फीटल इजेक्शन रेफ्लेक्स) किस हॉर्मोन के स्रवण को उद्दीपित करता है?
questions.text_english: Foetal ejection reflex in human female triggers the release of which hormone?

options.A: गर्भ की पीयूष ग्रंथि से ऑक्सीटोसिन

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D). The foetal ejection reflex is triggered by the fully developed foetus and the placenta. This signals the maternal pituitary gland to secrete oxytocin, which causes strong uterine contractions leading to parturition. The oxytocin then further stimulates the uterus in a positive feedback loop. hCG is produced early in pregnancy to maintain the corpus luteum; progesterone from corpus luteum maintains the uterine lining but is not released due to the foetal ejection reflex.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) है। गर्भ उत्क्षेपण प्रतिवर्ता के कारण माँ की पीयूष ग्रंथि से ऑक्सीटोसिन का स्राव होता है, जो गर्भाशय में प्रबल संकुचन उत्पन्न कर प्रसव (पार्चुरिशन) का कारण बनता है।

questions.text: कॉलम I में दी गई मदों का कॉलम II में दी गई मदों के साथ मिलान कीजिए तथा सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए। कॉलम I: a. केंचुआ, b. प्राणिप्लवक, c. पादपप्लवक, d. विलोमित (उल्टा) पिरैमिड। कॉलम II: i. जलीय पारितंत्र, ii. अपरदाहारी, iii. सागर में जैव मात्रा का पिरैमिड, iv. प्राथमिक उत्पादक।
questions.text_english: Match the items given in Column I with Column II and select the correct option. Column I: a. Earthworm, b. Zooplankton, c. Phytoplankton, d. Inverted pyramid. Column II: i. Aquatic Ecosystem, ii. Detritivore, iii. Pyramid of Biomass in Sea, iv. Primary Producer.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D): a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii. Earthworm (a) is a detritivore (ii) because it feeds on dead organic matter. Zooplankton (b) is found in aquatic ecosystems (i) as a consumer. Phytoplankton (c) is the primary producer (iv) in aquatic ecosystems. The inverted pyramid (d) refers to the pyramid of biomass in the sea (iii), where the biomass of producers (phytoplankton) is less than that of consumers (zooplankton) at any given time.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) है: a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii। केंचुआ अपरदाहारी है, प्राणिप्लवक जलीय पारितंत्र में पाया जाता है, पादपप्लवक प्राथमिक उत्पादक है, और सागर में उल्टा जैव मात्रा पिरैमिड पाया जाता है।

questions.text: कूटलेखन न करने वाले अव्यक्तेक (इंट्रॉन) तथा कूटलेखन करने वाले व्यक्तेक (एक्जॉन) युक्त जीन को कहते हैं:
questions.text_english: A gene having non-coding introns and coding exons is known as:
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Split gene. Eukaryotic genes contain non-coding sequences called introns interspersed with coding sequences called exons. Because the coding sequences are split by non-coding introns, such genes are called split genes. Pseudogenes are non-functional copies of genes. Structural genes code for proteins. Oncogenes are genes involved in cell cycle regulation that can cause cancer when mutated.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) विखंडित जीन है। सुकेन्द्रकी जीनों में गैर-कूटलेखन अनुक्रम (इंट्रॉन) और कूटलेखन अनुक्रम (एक्जॉन) दोनों होते हैं, इसलिए इन्हें विखंडित जीन कहते हैं।

questions.text: गोल्डन राइस एक उदीयमान पारजीनी फ़सल है। इसे जब खेतों में उगाने के लिए निर्मुक्त किया जाता है, तो यह सहायक होगी:
questions.text_english: Golden rice is a promising transgenic crop. When released for cultivation, it will help in:

options.A: पेट्रोल के समान ईंधन के उत्पादन में
options.B: मानव में विटामिन A की कमी को कम करने में

options_english.B: Reduction of Vitamin A deficiency in humans

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). Golden rice is a transgenic variety of rice engineered to produce beta-carotene (pro-vitamin A) in the endosperm, which gives it a characteristic golden colour. It was developed to address Vitamin A deficiency, especially in developing countries where rice is a staple food. It does not produce fuel, nor does it confer pest or herbicide resistance.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है। गोल्डन राइस को बीटा-कैरोटीन (विटामिन A का अग्रगामी) उत्पादन के लिए जनुकीय रूप से संशोधित किया गया है ताकि विटामिन A की कमी दूर हो सके।

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा ऐस्केरिएसिस (एस्केरिएसिस) का अभिलक्षण नहीं है?
questions.text_english: Which of the following is not a symptom of Ascariasis?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Skin ulcers. Ascariasis is caused by Ascaris lumbricoides (a roundworm) and its symptoms include intestinal obstruction, internal bleeding leading to anaemia, muscular pain, and fever. Skin ulcers are not a symptom of ascariasis; they are associated with diseases such as cutaneous leishmaniasis. Therefore, skin ulcers is the option that does NOT belong to ascariasis.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) त्वचीय व्रण है। एस्केरिएसिस के लक्षणों में आंत्र अवरोध, अरक्तता और पेशीय पीड़ा शामिल हैं, लेकिन त्वचीय व्रण इसका लक्षण नहीं है।

questions.text: अभिकथन (A): पुनरावृत्त अनुक्रम डीएनए अनुक्रम के खंड हैं जिनके बारे में माना जाता है कि उनका प्रकूट लेखन (कोडिंग) क्रिया से प्रत्यक्ष संबंध नहीं है। कारण (R): वे गुणसूत्रों (क्रोमोसोम) की संरचना, गतिकी तथा विकास पर प्रकाश डालते हैं।
questions.text_english: Assertion (A): Repetitive sequences are stretches of DNA sequences that are thought to have no direct coding functions. Reason (R): They shed light on chromosome structure, dynamics and evolution.
questions.instruction_line: निम्नलिखित कोड से सही उत्तर चुनिए: (A) दोनों सही, R, A की सही व्याख्या; (B) दोनों सही, R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं; (C) A सही, R गलत; (D) A गलत, R सही।
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer from codes: (A) Both true, R is correct explanation of A; (B) Both true, R is not correct explanation of A; (C) A is true, R is false; (D) A is false, R is true.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). The Assertion is true — repetitive sequences (satellite DNA) are non-coding stretches that do not directly participate in protein synthesis. The Reason is also true — repetitive sequences are indeed used to study chromosome structure, dynamics, and evolution (as used in DNA fingerprinting and phylogenetics). However, the Reason does not explain why repetitive sequences have no direct coding function; it merely states a separate use of these sequences. Hence both are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है। दोनों कथन सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता — कारण केवल इनके उपयोग को बताता है, न कि अकूटलेखन होने के कारण को।

questions.text: अभिकथन (A): नेट प्राथमिक उत्पादकता (एनपीपी) सदा ही सकल प्राथमिक उत्पादकता (जीपीपी) से कम होती है। कारण (R): सकल प्राथमिक उत्पादकता (जीपीपी) का कुछ अंश (मात्रा) पादपों द्वारा श्वसन हेतु उपयोग किया जाता है।
questions.text_english: Assertion (A): Net Primary Productivity (NPP) is always less than Gross Primary Productivity (GPP). Reason (R): A portion of Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) is used by plants for respiration.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). The Assertion is true — under normal conditions, DNA (being a large, hydrophilic, negatively charged molecule) cannot pass through the hydrophobic lipid bilayer of a bacterial cell membrane. The Reason is also true — DNA is indeed hydrophilic because of its phosphate backbone. Since the cell membrane is hydrophobic, the hydrophilic DNA is repelled and cannot cross it on its own; hence the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. In recombinant DNA technology, bacteria must be made competent by chemical or physical treatment to allow DNA entry.

sub_questions.solution: Agarose gel is a natural polysaccharide polymer extracted from red algae (sea weeds). It is used in electrophoresis because when set, it forms a mesh-like matrix with pores of specific sizes. As DNA fragments are negatively charged, they migrate through these pores towards the positive electrode under an electric field. Smaller fragments move faster and travel farther, while larger fragments move slowly, thus separating DNA fragments by their size.

sub_questions.solution: The most likely reason is that the DNA fragments were not stained. DNA is colourless and invisible under normal light. To make them visible, the gel is stained with ethidium bromide (EtBr), a dye that intercalates between the bases of DNA. When the stained gel is placed under ultraviolet (UV) light, the DNA fragments fluoresce as bright orange-red bands, making them visible.

The DNA is then extracted from this gel piece by a process called elution, in which the gel fragment is placed in an appropriate buffer and the DNA diffuses out. The eluted DNA can then be purified and used for further applications such as cloning or sequencing.

sub_questions.text_english: What is natural selection?

key_points: Natural selection is the process by which organisms with favourable variations survive and reproduce more successfully than those with less favourable variations
key_points_hindi: प्राकृतिक वरण वह प्रक्रिया है जिसमें अनुकूल विभिन्नताओं वाले जीव अधिक जीवित रहते हैं और प्रजनन करते हैं

sub_questions.solution: Natural selection is the process proposed by Charles Darwin in which organisms possessing favourable heritable variations survive better in their environment, reproduce successfully, and pass on these traits to the next generation, while those with unfavourable variations tend to perish. Over time, this leads to changes in the composition of a population.

sub_questions.text: उस प्रकार के प्राकृतिक वरण की व्याख्या कीजिए जो विकास के परिवर्तन को प्रोत्साहित करता है। उदाहरण दीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the type of natural selection that promotes evolutionary change. Give an example.

key_points: Directional selection promotes evolutionary change
It favours individuals at one extreme of a phenotypic range
Example: Industrial melanism in Biston betularia (peppered moth)
key_points_hindi: दिशात्मक वरण विकास को बढ़ावा देता है
उदाहरण: बिस्टन बेटुलेरिया में औद्योगिक मेलेनिज्म

sub_questions.solution: Directional selection is the type of natural selection that promotes evolutionary change. It operates when individuals at one extreme of the phenotypic range are favoured over those at the other extreme, causing the population mean to shift over generations. A classic example is industrial melanism in the peppered moth (Biston betularia). Before industrialisation, light-coloured moths were favoured because they were camouflaged against light-coloured tree bark. After industrialisation, soot darkened the tree bark, and dark-coloured (melanic) moths became better camouflaged, so they were favoured by natural selection and their frequency increased.

In this system, females are diploid (develop from fertilised eggs) and males are haploid (develop from unfertilised eggs by parthenogenesis). This pattern is characteristic of insects belonging to the order Hymenoptera, such as bees, ants, and wasps.

key_points_hindi: एलर्जी / अतिसंवेदनशीलता

sub_questions.solution: The condition is Allergy (Type I Hypersensitivity). The girl shows classic symptoms of an allergic reaction — sneezing, watery eyes, and difficulty in breathing — triggered by exposure to pollen from flowers.

sub_questions.text: इस अवस्था के लिए उत्तरदायी प्रतिरक्षा घटक का नाम लिखिए।

key_points: IgE (Immunoglobulin E)
key_points_hindi: IgE (इम्युनोग्लोब्युलिन E)

sub_questions.solution: The immune component responsible for allergy is IgE (Immunoglobulin E). IgE antibodies are produced in response to the allergen (pollen) and bind to receptors on mast cells and basophils, sensitising them for rapid degranulation upon re-exposure.

sub_questions.text: स्रावित होने वाले रसायन का नाम लिखिए।

key_points: Histamine
key_points_hindi: हिस्टामीन

sub_questions.solution: The chemical released is Histamine. When IgE-sensitised mast cells encounter the allergen again, they degranulate and release histamine, which causes the characteristic symptoms of allergy such as sneezing, watery eyes, and bronchoconstriction.

sub_questions.solution: Antihistamines are used to treat allergic reactions. Drugs such as cetirizine or loratadine block histamine receptors and relieve symptoms like sneezing, watery eyes, and breathing difficulty. Adrenaline (epinephrine) may be used in severe cases.

questions.text_english: A child is born with a genetic disorder due to the deletion of a gene. (a) Name such a gene studied by you. Explain how gene therapy can help in treating such a condition. (b) Mention one challenge associated with this therapy.

sub_questions.text: एक जीन का नाम लिखिए तथा जीन चिकित्सा की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Name a gene and explain how gene therapy can help.

key_points: ADA gene (Adenosine Deaminase gene)
A functional copy of the ADA gene is introduced into the patient's cells using a vector
The cells can then produce functional ADA enzyme
key_points_hindi: ADA जीन (एडिनोसिन डीएमिनेज)
वेक्टर द्वारा कार्यशील जीन रोगी की कोशिकाओं में प्रविष्ट कराई जाती है

sub_questions.solution: One such gene is the ADA gene, which codes for Adenosine Deaminase enzyme. Its deletion causes Severe Combined Immunodeficiency (SCID) in children. In gene therapy, lymphocytes are isolated from the patient's blood, and a functional copy of the ADA gene is introduced into these cells using a retroviral vector. The corrected cells are then returned to the patient's body, where they produce the functional ADA enzyme, restoring immune function. If the therapy is given at an early embryonic stage, it could be a permanent cure.

sub_questions.text: इस प्रकार के उपचार से संबद्ध एक चुनौती का उल्लेख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Mention one challenge associated with this therapy.

key_points: The therapy is not permanent since the genetically corrected lymphocytes are not immortal and the patient requires periodic infusions
key_points_hindi: यह उपचार स्थायी नहीं है क्योंकि संशोधित लिम्फोसाइट्स अल्पजीवी होते हैं और बार-बार उपचार की आवश्यकता होती है

sub_questions.solution: A major challenge associated with gene therapy using lymphocytes is that the procedure is not permanent. The genetically corrected lymphocytes are not long-lived, so the patient needs repeated treatment at intervals. For a permanent cure, the gene would need to be introduced into the bone marrow stem cells at an early embryonic stage.

questions.solution: A maize grain is a caryopsis (dry fruit) in which the pericarp is fused with the seed coat. questions.text_english: In vitro fertilization (IVF) is a popular method these days that is helping childless couples to bear a child. (a) Write the different steps that are carried out in this technique. (b) Would you consider gamete intra fallopian transfer as a type of IVF? Justify your answer.

sub_questions.text: आईवीएफ तकनीक के विभिन्न चरणों को लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Write the different steps carried out in IVF technique.

key_points: Ovarian stimulation and collection of ova from donor/wife
Collection and preparation of sperm sample
Fertilisation of egg with sperm outside the body (in vitro)
Development of embryo in culture medium
Embryo transfer (ET) into the uterus of the mother

sub_questions.solution: In IVF, the steps are as follows: first, the woman is given hormonal injections to stimulate superovulation so that multiple eggs are produced. These eggs are then surgically retrieved from the ovary. Simultaneously, sperm is collected from the male partner and processed. Fertilisation is carried out in a laboratory dish (in vitro), and the resulting zygotes are cultured into early embryos (up to 8-cell stage). Finally, the embryos are transferred into the uterus of the wife or surrogate mother, where implantation occurs and pregnancy proceeds normally.

sub_questions.text: क्या युग्मक अंतराफैलोपी स्थानांतरण को आईवीएफ का प्रकार माना जाएगा? स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Would you consider GIFT as a type of IVF? Justify.

key_points: No, GIFT is not a type of IVF
In GIFT, fertilisation occurs inside the fallopian tube (in vivo), not outside the body
IVF involves fertilisation outside the body (in vitro)

sub_questions.solution: No, Gamete Intra Fallopian Transfer (GIFT) is not a type of IVF. In IVF, fertilisation takes place outside the body (in vitro) in a laboratory dish. In GIFT, eggs collected from a donor or the wife's ovary are transferred directly into the fallopian tube along with the sperm, so fertilisation actually occurs inside the fallopian tube (in vivo). Since the fertilisation event itself is not in vitro, GIFT cannot be classified as a type of IVF.

questions.text_english: (a) Describe the experiment conducted by T.H. Morgan on Drosophila melanogaster involving eye colour and body colour. (b) How did the results deviate from Mendelian inheritance pattern? (c) Explain the two genetic terms used by Morgan for his observations.

sub_questions.text: मोर्गन के प्रयोग का वर्णन कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Describe Morgan's experiment.

key_points: Morgan crossed yellow-bodied white-eyed females with brown-bodied red-eyed males
F1 were brown-bodied red-eyed flies (wild type)
F1 females were test-crossed with yellow-bodied white-eyed males
Results showed more parental combinations and fewer recombinant combinations than expected

sub_questions.solution: Morgan performed dihybrid crosses in Drosophila melanogaster involving eye colour (white/red) and body colour (yellow/brown). He crossed yellow-bodied white-eyed females with brown-bodied red-eyed males. The F1 generation showed wild-type brown-bodied red-eyed flies, confirming dominance. When F1 females were test-crossed with yellow-bodied white-eyed males, the offspring showed a ratio that deviated from the expected 1:1:1:1 Mendelian ratio. Parental combinations (yellow-white and brown-red) appeared in much higher proportions than recombinant types (yellow-red and brown-white).

sub_questions.text: मेंडलीय वंशागति से विचलन की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: How did the results deviate from Mendelian inheritance pattern?

key_points: Expected 1:1:1:1 ratio for independent assortment was not obtained
Parental combinations appeared more frequently than recombinants
This is because genes for eye colour and body colour are linked on the same chromosome

sub_questions.solution: According to Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment, a test cross of a dihybrid should yield offspring in a 1:1:1:1 ratio. However, Morgan obtained far fewer recombinant types than expected. The parental combinations appeared in much greater frequency, which cannot be explained by independent assortment. This deviation occurred because the two genes (for eye colour and body colour) are located on the same chromosome and hence tend to be inherited together (they are linked).

sub_questions.text: मोर्गन द्वारा प्रयुक्त दो आनुवंशिक पदों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the two genetic terms used by Morgan for his observations.

key_points: Linkage — tendency of genes on the same chromosome to be inherited together
Recombination — production of new combinations of alleles due to crossing over during meiosis

sub_questions.solution: The two genetic terms used by Morgan are Linkage and Recombination. Linkage refers to the physical association of genes on the same chromosome, causing them to be inherited together more often than expected by chance. Recombination refers to the generation of new combinations of alleles due to crossing over (exchange of chromosomal segments) between homologous chromosomes during meiosis. Genes that are far apart on the same chromosome show more recombination, while those close together show less.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain the different ways by which apomictic seeds can be developed.

key_points: Diploid egg cell develops into embryo without fertilisation
Cells of the nucellus proliferate and develop into embryos (adventive embryony)
Both result in seeds that are genetically identical to the mother plant

sub_questions.solution: Apomixis is a form of asexual reproduction that produces seeds without fertilisation. It can occur in two main ways. First, the diploid megaspore mother cell or egg cell may develop into an embryo without undergoing meiosis or fertilisation — this is called diplospory. Second, cells of the nucellus (sporophytic tissue) may proliferate and differentiate into embryos, a process called adventive embryony (seen in citrus and mango). In both cases, the resulting seeds are genetically identical to the mother plant, producing true-breeding offspring.

sub_questions.text: किसानों के लिए असंगजनन बीजों का एक लाभ बताइए।
sub_questions.text_english: Mention one advantage of apomictic seeds for farmers.

key_points: Apomictic seeds preserve hybrid vigour (heterosis) over many generations, eliminating the need to buy new hybrid seeds every year
key_points_hindi: किसानों को हर वर्ष नए संकर बीज खरीदने की आवश्यकता नहीं पड़ती

sub_questions.solution: A major advantage of apomictic seeds for farmers is that they preserve hybrid vigour (heterosis) over successive generations. Since apomictic seeds produce offspring genetically identical to the mother plant, farmers can save and replant seeds without losing the advantageous traits, eliminating the expense of purchasing fresh hybrid seeds every cropping season.

sub_questions.text_english: What is meant by translation in protein synthesis?

key_points: Translation is the process of synthesising a polypeptide (protein) from the information encoded in mRNA
key_points_hindi: स्थानांतरण वह प्रक्रिया है जिसमें mRNA की आनुवंशिक सूचना के आधार पर पॉलीपेप्टाइड श्रृंखला का संश्लेषण होता है

sub_questions.solution: Translation in protein synthesis refers to the process by which the nucleotide sequence (genetic information) of a messenger RNA (mRNA) molecule is decoded by ribosomes to synthesise a specific polypeptide (protein) chain. It involves the sequential joining of amino acids as directed by codons on the mRNA, with the help of transfer RNA (tRNA) and ribosomes.

sub_questions.text: tRNA के आवेशीकरण (ऐमीनोऐसिडेशन) की व्याख्या कीजिए तथा इसके महत्त्व का उल्लेख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain charging of tRNA (aminoacylation) and mention its importance in translation.

key_points: Aminoacylation is the process of attaching a specific amino acid to its cognate tRNA
Catalysed by aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase using ATP energy
Importance: ensures the correct amino acid is delivered to the ribosome for the corresponding codon

sub_questions.solution: Charging of tRNA, also called aminoacylation, is the process of covalently attaching a specific amino acid to its corresponding tRNA molecule. This reaction is catalysed by a specific enzyme called aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase, which uses ATP energy to activate the amino acid and link it to the 3' CCA end of the tRNA. The resulting molecule is called charged tRNA or aminoacyl-tRNA. Its importance in translation is critical — the charged tRNA carries the correct amino acid to the ribosome, where the anticodon of the tRNA pairs with the complementary codon on the mRNA, ensuring that the amino acids are incorporated in the exact sequence specified by the genetic code.

Case II: A child is given rabies vaccine as a preventive measure. (a) Identify the type of immunity provided in both the cases. (b) Differentiate between the two types of immunity. (c) What is a vaccine? How does it help in preventing a disease?

sub_questions.text: दोनों केसों में प्रदान की गई प्रतिरक्षा के प्रकार को पहचानिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Identify the type of immunity in both cases.

key_points: Case I: Passive immunity (ready-made antibodies given)
Case II: Active immunity (vaccine stimulates body to produce antibodies)
key_points_hindi: केस I: निष्क्रिय प्रतिरक्षा
केस II: सक्रिय प्रतिरक्षा

sub_questions.solution: In Case I, the person is given an antitoxin (pre-formed antibodies), which provides Passive Immunity — ready-made antibodies are directly introduced into the body. In Case II, the child is given a vaccine, which stimulates the child's own immune system to produce antibodies, providing Active Immunity.

sub_questions.text: दोनों प्रकार की प्रतिरक्षा के बीच विभेद कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Differentiate between active and passive immunity.

key_points: Active immunity: slow, long-lasting, produced by body itself; Passive immunity: fast, short-lived, antibodies given from outside

sub_questions.solution: Active immunity develops when the body's own immune system produces antibodies in response to an antigen (natural infection or vaccine). It is slow to develop (takes days to weeks) but provides long-lasting protection due to immunological memory. Passive immunity is obtained when ready-made antibodies (antitoxins or immune sera) are injected from an external source. It provides immediate protection but is short-lived because no memory cells are formed.

sub_questions.text: टीका क्या है? रोग नियंत्रण में यह कैसे सहायक है?
sub_questions.text_english: What is a vaccine? How does it help in preventing a disease?

key_points: A vaccine is a preparation of weakened/killed pathogens or their antigens/toxoids
It stimulates the immune system to produce antibodies and memory cells
On subsequent exposure to the actual pathogen, the immune system responds rapidly and prevents disease

sub_questions.solution: A vaccine is a biological preparation containing weakened (attenuated) or killed pathogens, their surface antigens, or inactivated toxins (toxoids). When injected into a person, the vaccine stimulates the immune system to produce specific antibodies and memory B and T cells against those antigens. If the person is later exposed to the actual pathogen, the memory cells mount a rapid and strong secondary immune response, producing large amounts of antibodies that neutralise the pathogen before it can cause disease, thereby preventing infection.

sub_questions.text_english: What is the carrying capacity of a species in a habitat?

key_points: Carrying capacity (K) is the maximum population size of a species that a given habitat can support sustainably with available resources
key_points_hindi: पोषण क्षमता (K) वह अधिकतम जनसंख्या आकार है जिसे एक आवास संसाधनों की उपलब्धता के आधार पर दीर्घकाल तक संभाल सकता है

sub_questions.solution: The carrying capacity (K) of a species in a habitat is the maximum population size that can be sustained indefinitely in a given environment with the available food, space, water, and other resources. Beyond this limit, the environment cannot support further population growth due to resource depletion.

sub_questions.text: पोषण क्षमता को ध्यान में रखने वाले वृद्धि वक्र की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the growth curve that takes carrying capacity into account.

key_points: Logistic growth curve (S-shaped / sigmoid curve)
Population grows slowly initially (lag phase), then rapidly (exponential phase), then slows down as it approaches K
The equation is dN/dt = rN(K-N)/K

sub_questions.solution: The growth curve that takes carrying capacity into account is the Logistic Growth Curve, also called the S-shaped or Sigmoid curve. When a population is introduced into a new environment with limited resources, it first shows a slow initial growth (lag phase) as individuals get established. Then growth accelerates rapidly (exponential phase). As the population approaches the carrying capacity (K), intraspecific competition for limited resources intensifies, growth rate slows down, and finally the population stabilises near K. The logistic growth is described by the equation dN/dt = rN(K-N)/K, where r is the intrinsic rate of natural increase and N is the current population size. The population never exceeds K in an ideal logistic growth model.

key_points: At 10 minutes, nicotine concentration is at its peak — approximately 45 mg/cm³
This is because the smoker has been inhaling 10 puffs/minute for 10 consecutive minutes, causing nicotine to accumulate in the blood to its maximum level

sub_questions.solution: At 10 minutes, the concentration of nicotine in the blood reaches its maximum value of approximately 45 mg/cm³. This peak occurs because the smoker has been continuously inhaling 10 puffs per minute for 10 minutes. Nicotine is rapidly absorbed into the bloodstream through the lungs with each puff, and since the rate of absorption exceeds the rate of metabolism during smoking, nicotine accumulates progressively in the blood until it reaches its highest concentration at 10 minutes when smoking ceases.

sub_questions.text: इस धूम्रपान के 10 मिनट पर कार्बन मोनोक्साइड तथा हीमआबद्ध ऑक्सीजन की सांद्रता किस प्रकार प्रभावित होगी?
sub_questions.text_english: How will this affect the concentration of carbon monoxide and haem-bound oxygen at 10 minutes?

key_points: Carbon monoxide concentration in blood will be high at 10 minutes
Haem-bound oxygen will be low because CO binds to haemoglobin with much higher affinity than O₂, forming carboxyhaemoglobin
key_points_hindi: CO की सांद्रता अधिक होगी; हीम-आबद्ध ऑक्सीजन कम होगी

sub_questions.solution: At 10 minutes of smoking, the concentration of carbon monoxide (CO) in the blood will be at its highest, because CO from cigarette smoke accumulates in the blood with continued smoking. As a consequence, the concentration of haem-bound oxygen will be significantly reduced, because CO has a far greater affinity (about 200 times more) for haemoglobin than oxygen. CO binds to haemoglobin forming carboxyhaemoglobin (COHb), which cannot carry oxygen. This reduces the oxygen-carrying capacity of blood and leads to hypoxia.

sub_questions.text: सिगरेट के धूम्रपान के परिणामस्वरूप उच्च रक्तचाप (दाब) तथा हृदय स्पंदन की दर में वृद्धि कैसे हो जाती है?
sub_questions.text_english: How does cigarette smoking result in high blood pressure and increase in heart rate?

key_points: Nicotine stimulates the adrenal glands to release adrenaline and nor-adrenaline
These hormones increase heart rate and cause vasoconstriction, raising blood pressure

sub_questions.solution: Cigarette smoking leads to high blood pressure and increased heart rate primarily because nicotine stimulates the adrenal medulla to release adrenaline (epinephrine) and nor-adrenaline (norepinephrine) into the bloodstream. These catecholamine hormones act on the heart to increase the rate and force of contractions, and cause vasoconstriction (narrowing of blood vessels). The combined effect of faster heart rate and narrower blood vessels results in elevated blood pressure.

sub_questions.solution: Nicotine belongs to the class of drugs called alkaloids, which are nitrogen-containing organic compounds derived from plants and act as stimulants on the nervous system. Another drug belonging to the same class (alkaloids/stimulants) is caffeine (found in tea and coffee) or cocaine (derived from Erythroxylum coca). These alkaloids share the property of stimulating the central nervous system, increasing alertness, and causing addiction.

sub_questions.text_english: Which method conserves the highest number of species? Is it ex situ or in situ conservation?

In situ conservation involves protecting species in their natural habitat, allowing them to live and evolve in their natural ecosystem. In contrast, ex situ conservation involves removing organisms from their natural habitat and maintaining them under artificial or controlled conditions such as zoos, botanical gardens, seed banks, or cryopreservation facilities. In situ conservation preserves entire ecosystems, while ex situ focuses on individual species or populations outside their native environment.

They act as biodiversity repositories and help maintain ecological balance in the surrounding landscape.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain any two basic principles/core techniques on which biotechnology is based.

key_points: Genetic engineering (manipulation of genes to alter phenotype)
Maintenance of sterile conditions to enable microorganism growth for industrial production

sub_questions.solution: Biotechnology is based on two core principles. The first is Genetic Engineering, which involves the manipulation of gene expression to alter the phenotype of an organism. This includes techniques such as recombinant DNA technology, gene cloning, and gene editing that allow scientists to introduce, delete, or modify specific genes in an organism to achieve desired traits. The second core principle is the maintenance of sterile (aseptic) conditions, which is essential when culturing microorganisms or cells for large-scale industrial production of useful products like vaccines, enzymes, and antibiotics, preventing contamination from undesired organisms.

sub_questions.text_english: Describe any three key tools used in Recombinant DNA technology.

key_points: Restriction endonucleases — cut DNA at specific sequences
Cloning vectors (plasmids, bacteriophages) — carry and replicate foreign DNA in host cells
Host organism — allows replication and expression of recombinant DNA

sub_questions.solution: Three key tools used in Recombinant DNA technology are: (1) Restriction Endonucleases — these are molecular scissors that cut DNA at specific palindromic sequences, producing defined fragments with either blunt or sticky ends. Different restriction enzymes recognise different sequences, allowing precise cutting of DNA. (2) Cloning Vectors — these are DNA molecules such as plasmids, bacteriophages (lambda phage), or cosmids that act as vehicles to carry foreign DNA into a host cell. A vector must have an origin of replication, selectable markers (antibiotic resistance genes), and cloning sites. (3) Host Organisms — commonly bacteria like E. coli, which take up the recombinant vector through transformation, replicate it along with their own DNA, and can be induced to express the inserted gene, producing the desired protein product in large quantities.

sub_questions.text_english: Name conventional methods of diagnosis and their disadvantages.

key_points: Conventional methods: clinical examination (symptoms), biochemical analysis (blood/urine tests)
Limitations: not sensitive enough for early detection; cannot detect disease at the molecular or sub-clinical stage; time-consuming and sometimes give false results

sub_questions.solution: Conventional methods of disease diagnosis include clinical examination (based on signs and symptoms observed by a physician) and biochemical analysis such as blood tests, urine analysis, and microscopic examination of pathogens. Their limitations are that they are often not sensitive enough to detect a disease at an early stage, before symptoms appear. By the time a disease is diagnosed through conventional methods, significant tissue damage may already have occurred. These methods also cannot distinguish between closely related pathogens and may give false positive or false negative results.

sub_questions.text: जैव-प्रौद्योगिकी द्वारा विकसित तीन नैदानिक तकनीकों की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain three biotechnology-based diagnostic techniques.

key_points: ELISA — detects antigens or antibodies using enzyme-tagged antibodies
PCR — amplifies pathogen DNA for detection even at very low concentrations
DNA probe / Recombinant DNA based techniques — identifies specific nucleotide sequences of pathogens

sub_questions.solution: Three biotechnology-based diagnostic techniques are: (1) ELISA (Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay) — this technique uses enzyme-tagged antibodies to detect specific antigens (from pathogens) or antibodies (produced by the patient's immune system) in blood or tissue samples. The enzyme produces a colour change in the presence of its substrate, indicating a positive result. It is used to detect HIV, hepatitis B, and other infections. (2) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) — this technique amplifies even a single copy of pathogen DNA (or RNA after converting to cDNA) billions of times in a few hours. It can detect the presence of a pathogen's genetic material with extreme sensitivity and specificity, even before symptoms appear. It is used to diagnose HIV, TB, COVID-19, and genetic disorders. (3) DNA Probe/Hybridisation Technique — a single-stranded DNA fragment complementary to the pathogen's specific gene is labelled with a radioactive or fluorescent marker. When hybridised with a patient sample, it binds specifically to the target DNA, indicating the presence of the pathogen. This technique is highly specific and is used to identify genetic diseases and infections.

sub_questions.text_english: Describe Griffith's experiments and comment on the significance of results.

key_points: Injected live S strain (smooth, virulent) into mice — mice died
Injected live R strain (rough, non-virulent) — mice survived
Injected heat-killed S strain — mice survived
Injected mixture of live R + heat-killed S — mice died and live S bacteria recovered
Conclusion: a transforming principle passed from dead S to live R cells

sub_questions.solution: Frederick Griffith conducted a series of experiments in 1928 using Streptococcus pneumoniae. When he injected live smooth (S) strain bacteria (virulent, with a polysaccharide capsule) into mice, all mice died. When he injected live rough (R) strain bacteria (non-virulent, no capsule), the mice survived. When he injected heat-killed S strain bacteria alone, the mice survived. However, when he injected a mixture of live R strain and heat-killed S strain into mice, the mice died, and live S strain bacteria were recovered from their blood. Griffith concluded that some 'transforming principle' had passed from the heat-killed S strain to the living R strain, converting (transforming) it into virulent S strain bacteria. The significance of this result is that it first demonstrated that heritable characteristics could be transferred between organisms (transformation), and that the hereditary material (transforming principle) was a chemical entity that could be experimentally manipulated.

sub_questions.text: एवेरी, मैक्लिओड तथा मैक्काटी के योगदान का उल्लेख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: State the contribution of Avery, MacLeod and McCarty.

key_points: They identified that the transforming principle in Griffith's experiment was DNA, not protein or RNA
They treated the S strain extract with DNase, RNase, and protease separately; only DNase destroyed the transforming ability

sub_questions.solution: Avery, MacLeod, and McCarty (1944) designed a series of biochemical experiments to identify the chemical nature of Griffith's transforming principle. They extracted the components from heat-killed S strain cells and treated separate samples with DNase (destroys DNA), RNase (destroys RNA), and protease (destroys proteins). They found that only treatment with DNase abolished the transforming ability of the extract, while RNase and protease treatments had no effect. This definitively proved that DNA — not protein or RNA — was the transforming principle and therefore the genetic material. Their work provided the first direct biochemical evidence that DNA is the molecule of heredity.

questions.text: (ख) निम्नलिखित प्रश्न हीमोफीलिया पर आधारित (संबंधित) हैं। (i) निम्नलिखित के बीच क्रॉस बनाइए: (I) एक सामान्य स्त्री तथा हीमोफीलिक पुरुष; (II) संवाहक स्त्री तथा सामान्य पुरुष; (III) संवाहक स्त्री तथा हीमोफीलिक पुरुष। (ii) उपर्युक्त क्रॉसों के आधार पर अपने निष्कर्ष लिखिए। इस विकार (रोग) की वंशागति के प्रकार पर टिप्पणी कीजिए। (प्रयोग कीजिए: X – सामान्य, Xh – हीमोफीलिक)

sub_questions.text_english: Cross I: Normal female × Haemophilic male.

key_points: Parents: XX (normal female) × XhY (haemophilic male)
Offspring: XXh (carrier female), XY (normal male), XXh (carrier female), XY (normal male)
Ratio: 50% carrier females, 50% normal males; all phenotypically normal

sub_questions.solution: Cross I: Normal female (XX) × Haemophilic male (XhY). Gametes from female: X, X. Gametes from male: Xh, Y. Offspring: XXh (carrier female), XY (normal male), XXh (carrier female), XY (normal male). All daughters are phenotypically normal but are carriers (XXh), and all sons are phenotypically normal (XY). None of the offspring shows haemophilia in this cross.

sub_questions.text: संवाहक स्त्री × सामान्य पुरुष का क्रॉस बनाइए।
sub_questions.text_english: Cross II: Carrier female × Normal male.

key_points: Parents: XXh (carrier female) × XY (normal male)
Offspring: XX (normal female), XXh (carrier female), XY (normal male), XhY (haemophilic male)
50% normal females and carriers; 50% normal and haemophilic males

sub_questions.solution: Cross II: Carrier female (XXh) × Normal male (XY). Gametes from female: X, Xh. Gametes from male: X, Y. Offspring: XX (normal female), XXh (carrier female), XY (normal male), XhY (haemophilic male). Result: 25% normal females, 25% carrier females, 25% normal males, 25% haemophilic males. This cross shows that sons have a 50% chance of being haemophilic.

sub_questions.text: संवाहक स्त्री × हीमोफीलिक पुरुष का क्रॉस बनाइए।
sub_questions.text_english: Cross III: Carrier female × Haemophilic male.

key_points: Parents: XXh (carrier female) × XhY (haemophilic male)
Offspring: XXh (carrier female), XhXh (haemophilic female), XY (normal male), XhY (haemophilic male)
50% haemophilic offspring including haemophilic females

sub_questions.solution: Cross III: Carrier female (XXh) × Haemophilic male (XhY). Gametes from female: X, Xh. Gametes from male: Xh, Y. Offspring: XXh (carrier female), XhXh (haemophilic female), XY (normal male), XhY (haemophilic male). Result: 25% carrier females, 25% haemophilic females, 25% normal males, 25% haemophilic males. This is the only cross where haemophilic females (XhXh) can appear.

sub_questions.text: क्रॉसों से निष्कर्ष लिखिए तथा वंशागति के प्रकार पर टिप्पणी कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Write conclusions from crosses and comment on the type of inheritance.

key_points: Haemophilia is an X-linked recessive disorder
Females require two copies of the defective allele to be affected; males need only one
Carrier females (XXh) are phenotypically normal but can transmit the disease to sons

sub_questions.solution: From these crosses, it is clear that haemophilia is an X-linked recessive disorder. Sons of carrier mothers have a 50% chance of being haemophilic (Cross II), while daughters of carrier mothers have a 50% chance of being carriers. Haemophilic females (XhXh) can only arise when both the mother is a carrier and the father is haemophilic (Cross III), which is rare. This type of inheritance is called X-linked recessive inheritance — the gene is located on the X chromosome, males (XY) are more frequently affected because they have only one X chromosome, while females (XX) are usually carriers unless homozygous for the allele.

sub_questions.text: शुक्रजनक नलिका का स्वच्छ आरेख बनाइए तथा पाँच भागों को नामांकित कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Draw a neat sectional view of seminiferous tubule showing spermatogenesis and label five stages.

key_points: Spermatogonia (diploid, outer layer)
Primary spermatocytes (undergoing meiosis I)
Secondary spermatocytes (after meiosis I, haploid)
Spermatids (after meiosis II)
Spermatozoa (mature sperm cells)
Sertoli cells (nurse cells supporting development)

sub_questions.solution: A sectional view of the seminiferous tubule should show the following (from periphery to lumen): the basement membrane, spermatogonia (diploid stem cells at the periphery), primary spermatocytes (undergoing meiosis I), secondary spermatocytes (haploid, after meiosis I), spermatids (after meiosis II, undergoing spermiogenesis), and mature spermatozoa (near the lumen). Sertoli cells extend from the basement membrane to the lumen and provide nourishment to developing germ cells. Any five of these labelled parts are acceptable.

sub_questions.text: मानव में शुक्रजनन के हॉर्मोनी नियमन की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain the hormonal regulation of spermatogenesis in humans.

key_points: Hypothalamus releases GnRH, which stimulates anterior pituitary
Anterior pituitary secretes FSH and LH
FSH stimulates Sertoli cells to support spermatogenesis; LH stimulates Leydig cells to produce testosterone
Testosterone is necessary for the completion of spermatogenesis

sub_questions.solution: Spermatogenesis in humans is regulated by a hormonal axis. The hypothalamus secretes Gonadotropin Releasing Hormone (GnRH), which acts on the anterior pituitary gland and stimulates it to secrete two gonadotropins: Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH) and Luteinizing Hormone (LH). FSH acts on Sertoli cells of the seminiferous tubule, stimulating them to secrete androgen binding protein (ABP) and other factors that support the growth and nutrition of developing sperm cells. LH acts on Leydig cells (interstitial cells) in the testis, stimulating them to produce the male sex hormone testosterone. Testosterone is essential for the completion of spermatogenesis, especially for the later stages of differentiation and spermiation. High levels of testosterone also inhibit further GnRH and LH secretion through negative feedback.

questions.text: (ख) सगर्भता का चिकित्सीय समापन (एमटीपी) जनन स्वास्थ्य में एक महत्त्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाता है। (i) एमटीपी क्या है? (ii) भारत में किन परिस्थितियों में इस तकनीक को वैधानिक स्वीकृति दी गई है? किन्हीं दो बिंदुओं का उल्लेख कीजिए। (iii) सगर्भता की किस अवधि तक एमटीपी को वैधानिक तथा चिकित्सीय रूप से सुरक्षित माना गया है? Mention any two points. (iii) In which stage of pregnancy is MTP considered legally and medically safe? (iv) Explain any two risks/concerns associated with this process.

sub_questions.text: एमटीपी क्या है?
sub_questions.text_english: What is MTP?

key_points: MTP is the deliberate termination (induced abortion) of a pregnancy before it reaches full term
key_points_hindi: एमटीपी गर्भावस्था का जानबूझकर किया गया चिकित्सीय समापन है

sub_questions.solution: Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) is the deliberate and intentional termination of a pregnancy before the foetus reaches full term, carried out by a qualified medical practitioner. It involves the removal or expulsion of the developing embryo or foetus from the uterus by medical or surgical means.

sub_questions.text: भारत में एमटीपी की वैधानिक अनुमति किन दो परिस्थितियों में दी गई है?
sub_questions.text_english: Under what two conditions is MTP legally permitted in India?

key_points: When continuation of pregnancy poses a risk to the physical or mental health of the mother
When the pregnancy is a result of rape or failure of contraception (unwanted pregnancy)

sub_questions.solution: In India, under the Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act (1971, amended 2021), MTP is legally permitted under the following two conditions (among others): first, when the continuation of the pregnancy would involve a grave risk to the life of the pregnant woman or cause substantial injury to her physical or mental health; and second, when the pregnancy has resulted from the failure of contraceptive devices or rape, making it an unwanted pregnancy. MTP is also permitted when there is substantial risk that the child, if born, would suffer from serious physical or mental abnormalities.

sub_questions.text: सगर्भता की किस अवधि तक एमटीपी वैधानिक और चिकित्सीय रूप से सुरक्षित है?
sub_questions.text_english: In which stage of pregnancy is MTP considered legally and medically safe?

key_points: MTP is considered safe up to the first trimester (up to 12 weeks of pregnancy)
Under amended law (2021), it can extend to 20–24 weeks under specific conditions with approval

sub_questions.solution: MTP is considered legally and medically safe during the first trimester, i.e., up to 12 weeks of pregnancy. During this period, the procedure is relatively simple, safe, and carries fewer risks. Under the amended MTP Act 2021, the upper limit can be extended to 20 weeks (with one doctor's approval) and up to 24 weeks in special categories such as survivors of rape, with approval from a Medical Board.

sub_questions.text: एमटीपी से संबंधित दो खतरों/चिंताओं की व्याख्या कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Explain any two risks/concerns associated with MTP.

key_points: Misuse for sex-selective abortion leading to female foeticide and skewed sex ratio
Medical risks of unsafe/illegal abortions — haemorrhage, infection, and maternal mortality

sub_questions.solution: Two major risks and concerns associated with MTP are: first, misuse for sex-selective abortions — MTP is sometimes used illegally for female foeticide (aborting female foetuses after sex determination), which has led to a severely skewed sex ratio in parts of India. This is a serious ethical, social, and legal concern. Second, health risks from unsafe abortions — when MTPs are performed by unqualified practitioners or in unhygienic conditions (illegal abortions), they can lead to serious complications including haemorrhage (excessive bleeding), uterine perforation, septicaemia (blood infection), and even maternal death. This is especially a concern in countries or regions where legal access to safe abortion is restricted.
